note: Short questions on scheduled releases. Rules: questions/README.md. A question is never edited after it is written; only its outcome is filled in.

question.en: Will the November unemployment rate be 4.2% or higher?

questions.reading: Unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, as first printed in the release for November 2026.
questions.basis: The rate was 4.1% in October and BLS says it has stayed between 4.1% and 4.3% since March. A rounded rate moves up by a tenth or more in roughly one month in three, and payrolls were firm in October.

question.en: Will November payrolls rise by 100,000 or more?

questions.reading: Change in total nonfarm payroll employment, seasonally adjusted, in thousands, as first printed for November 2026. Later revisions do not count.
questions.basis: October was +165,000, August +186,000 and September +60,000 after revision, but the 12-month average is only +48,000. The first print swings by tens of thousands on sampling alone, so this is close to even.

question.en: Will average hourly earnings rise 0.4% or more on the month?
question.ko: 시간당 평균 임금이 전월보다 0.4% 이상 오를까요?

questions.reading: Average hourly earnings of all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, percent change from the prior month as stated in the release text for November 2026.
questions.basis: October was +0.4%, but the 12-month rise of 3.1% works out to about 0.26% a month. A second 0.4% in a row would be well above that pace.

question.en: Will the Fed raise its target range on December 9?

questions.reading: Change in the upper bound of the federal funds target range in the statement of the December 8-9 meeting, in percentage points. An increase of 0.25 or more counts as yes.

previous.period: October 27-28 meeting (held at 3.75% to 4.00%, two votes for an increase)

questions.basis: Two members already voted to raise in October, PCE inflation went from 3.6% to 3.8%, and the minutes say futures gave high odds to a rise by year-end. This number mostly follows what markets already price; AFMX has not read the futures itself.

question.en: Will November consumer prices rise 0.4% or more on the month?

questions.reading: CPI-U, all items, seasonally adjusted percent change from the prior month, as first printed for November 2026.
questions.basis: Four of the last seven months were 0.4% or more, mostly when energy jumped. Gasoline fell 0.7% before seasonal adjustment in October. AFMX has not read November fuel prices, so this is the recent rate shaded down a little.

question.en: Will November core consumer prices rise 0.3% or more on the month?

questions.reading: CPI-U, all items less food and energy, seasonally adjusted percent change from the prior month, as first printed for November 2026.
questions.basis: Core rose 0.3% in each of August, September and October, with shelter at 0.3% to 0.4%. Four of the last seven months were 0.3% or more.
